characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Demonstrates technical feasibility of platform-neutral Danish digital identity through two non-production, standards-based demonstrators—one FIDO2-on-GrapheneOS mobile example and one browser-based or hardware-token fallback. Success means delivering working prototypes by month 16 and obtaining independent security review, proving secure, open-standard authentication paths exist without exclusive Apple/Google dependence. Metrics include demonstrator functionality, standards compliance verification, and expert validation reports.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Enables Procurement Influence Strategy by providing concrete architectural evidence and cost/feasibility data that procurement teams can reference to justify platform-neutral requirements, making supplier-diversity language technically defensible and less easily dismissed.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Constrains EU Standards Engagement Strategy due to specialized engineering capacity requirements; simultaneous deep EU standards participation diverts technical staff from demonstrator polish and security review, forcing deferred EU engagement or reduced local demonstrator maturity.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Shapes procurement and policy debate by reframing platform dependency as a domestic resilience, continuity-of-service, and supplier-concentration risk—not ideology or privacy alone. Success means submitting formal policy proposals to Digitaliseringsstyrelsen by month 6, securing written institutional responses by month 16, and embedding platform-neutrality language in at least one official AltID document by month 24. Metrics include institutional engagement frequency, proposal uptake, and procurement document amendments.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Enables Coalition Building Strategy by establishing pragmatic, non-ideological framing (continuity, procurement neutrality, supplier risk) that appeals to institutional stakeholders beyond privacy advocates, broadening coalition legitimacy and reducing perception as niche activism.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Constrains EU Standards Engagement Strategy through messaging specialization; emphasizing Danish sovereignty and national procurement resilience may reduce appeal to EU partners prioritizing harmonized, cross-border standards, requiring separate EU-targeted messaging and dividing advocacy narrative bandwidth.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Builds and sustains multi-stakeholder coalition spanning security experts, civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academics, contingency planners, and sympathetic Folketinget members to amplify platform-neutrality advocacy through diverse messengers. Success means identifying and coordinating at least 8–10 committed partners by month 8, maintaining alignment despite conflicting priorities, and achieving visible joint statements or publications. Key metrics include stakeholder diversity, public coordination frequency, and demonstrated collective advocacy impact on policy discussions.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Enables Policy Advocacy Strategy by diversifying credibility and reach—academic and civil-society voices collectively outweigh narrow technical lobbying, making platform-neutrality arguments harder for incumbents to marginalize, and amplifies Procurement Influence Strategy by providing institutional coalition partners who can directly engage procurement authorities.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Constrains Technical Feasibility Strategy through engagement overhead; broader coalition coordination demands policy staff for stakeholder management and visibility, potentially diverting resources from engineering work and creating organizational pressure to prioritize coalition messaging over demonstrator technical rigor and security review depth.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Embeds platform-neutrality, fallback access, and supplier-concentration risk language into AltID and related procurement cycles, targeting official requirements and scoring criteria. Success requires procurement-ready language drafts by month 18, institutional adoption of platform-neutral provisions by month 22, and inclusion of supplier-diversity or fallback-access language in at least one formal AltID procurement or design document by month 24. Metrics include procurement document amendments, vendor guidance alignment, and institutional adoption frequency.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Enables Technical Feasibility Strategy by converting demonstrator evidence into procurement evaluation criteria, and amplifies Coalition Building Strategy by providing institutional coalition partners with defensible, standards-aligned rationale for including supplier-diversity and fallback-access requirements, strengthening their negotiating position.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Constrains EU Standards Engagement Strategy through jurisdictional and timing focus; securing Danish procurement traction by month 18 requires concentrated institutional engagement, reducing capacity for sustained EU standards participation which operates on longer, less-synchronized decision cycles and requires parallel messaging infrastructure.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Extends platform-neutrality advocacy to European Digital Identity Wallet and eIDAS2 standards, aligning Danish resilience arguments with broader European interoperability, portability, and lock-in-reduction requirements. Success means contributing technical and policy input to relevant EU working groups by month 20, achieving explicit platform-neutral or fallback-access language in at least one official EU Digital Identity Wallet material by month 24, and fostering cross-member-state coordination on sovereign digital identity resilience. Metrics include EU working-group participation frequency, contributed language adoption, and cross-border alignment.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Amplifies Policy Advocacy Strategy by elevating Danish arguments to European regulatory scale, ensuring domestic procurement language aligns with EU standards momentum, and strengthens Technical Feasibility Strategy by providing international validation audiences and comparative interoperability benchmarks for demonstrators.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Constrains Procurement Influence Strategy through resource allocation and timing; deep EU working-group participation (drafting proposals, attending meetings, coordinating member states) competes directly with concentrated domestic stakeholder engagement required for Danish AltID procurement traction before month 18.
